nora (VectorMaps): Hi folks, hitting a blocker after we switched our embeddings pipeline to int8. Some responses are twice the expected length and our downstream indexer rejects them. Error from our service: `RuntimeError: embedding size 1024 != expected 512`. We didn't change the indexer. Any clues?

 diego - Support: thanks for flagging—sorry about the hit. quick ones: which model id in the request, and can you paste the request_id from the error? also did you rotate any model alias or update the model name in env?

 nora (VectorMaps): request_id `rv_20250403_aabbcc`. Payload: ```json
{"model":"open-embed-medium-int8","input":["tile_123","tile_124"],"options":{"batch_size":16}}
``` error: ```
HTTP 400 \n{"error":"embedding_dimension_mismatch","expected":512,"received":1024,"request_id":"rv_20250403_aabbcc"}
``` We used to get 512 with fp16. thought int8 only affects precision.

 anya - ML Eng: short answer: quantization (fp16->int8) should not change vector length. long answer: when creating quantized artifacts we sometimes build from a different base checkpoint by mistake, or the packaging script accidentally concatenated two projection heads for a particular family. both cases would double the dim. can you call the model metadata endpoint? `GET /v1/models/open-embed-medium-int8/metadata` should show `embedding_dim`.

 nora (VectorMaps): ran it, response: ```json
{"model":"open-embed-medium-int8","embedding_dim":1024,"quantization":"int8","built_at":"2025-03-29T22:11:00Z"}
``` but the canonical `open-embed-medium@v2` shows 512. weird.

 ops-bot: deployment change CL-7920 applied 2025-03-29T22:10:12Z to model packaging pipeline. Related PR: repo:packaging #457.

 anya - ML Eng: that matches a packaging regression we rolled. impact: some int8 artifacts were created from a larger base model accidentally. root cause tracked in INT-SYS-1227. For mitigation: 1) short-term: switch your calls to the unquantized `open-embed-medium@v2` (same shape you expect); 2) we can rebuild `open-embed-medium-int8` from the correct checkpoint and validate shape before release; 3) if you'd rather keep using the 1024 artifact, update your indexer schema (not recommended).

 nora (VectorMaps): we want to keep int8 for latency/cost. how long to rebuild and how will we verify shape? also FYI when we sent batch_size=16 we saw inconsistent lengths inside the same response occasionally (some items 512, some 1024) which created havoc. could that be a batching bug?

 diego - Support: batching inconsistencies are definitely alarming. possible causes: mixed model alias resolution within a sharded serving pool (some shards running the old artifact, some new); or a conversion script that left mixed projections in the same artifact. We'll open an infra trace for your req id. Meanwhile please try sending non-batched single inputs to see if the shape is stable for individual calls.

 ops-bot: trace ticket TRC-4417 created for request rv_20250403_aabbcc, assigned to infra-packaging.

 anya - ML Eng: rebuild plan: we can produce a new int8 artifact from the canonical `open-embed-medium@v2` checkpoint, run the unit check that asserts `embedding_dim == metadata.embedding_dim`, and run a small smoke eval with your sample inputs. ETA: 24-36 hours if prioritized. We will also add a gating test to the packaging pipeline to prevent aliasing mismatches.

 nora (VectorMaps): thanks. i'll DM a small sample set and the indexer logs. One more question: are there cases where quantization transforms like per-channel vs per-tensor quantization change the output vector length due to fused ops or packing?

 anya - ML Eng: good question. No — quantization formats (per-channel vs per-tensor) and kernel fusions affect numeric representation and performance but not the output embedding dimensionality. The only ways the length changes are architectural (different projection matrix sizes), concatenating heads, or accidentally using a bigger model checkpoint. We've seen a separate bug where a conversion tool wrote two projection outputs to the same output tensor, but that's more of a tool bug (we fixed it in CL-7683). We'll double-check that your artifact doesn't have mixed outputs.

 nora (VectorMaps): i tried single-input calls and they consistently return 1024 from `open-embed-medium-int8`. switched to `open-embed-medium@v2` and got 512 as expected. we'll switch to the @v2 for now in prod. please prioritize rebuild.

 diego - Support: noted. next steps for us: 1) infra will queue rebuild from correct checkpoint (JOB-5602), run shape validation harness, and deploy to staging; 2) we'll run your samples against the staging artifact and share logs; 3) add a packaging-gate test to compare metadata.embedding_dim to a small-run output.shape. internal ticket: SPT-3399 (customer-impact).

 ops-bot: JOB-5602 queued by infra-packaging.

 anya - ML Eng: we'll also add an extra CI check to catch mixed shapes in batch outputs. regarding your earlier batching inconsistency, that likely came from a rolling rollout where some hosts had the repaired artifact and others hadn't. once we stabilize the alias mapping and finish rebuild, that should stop.

 nora (VectorMaps): switching to @v2 now. please confirm rebuild and we'll test once you have staging up. thanks for the quick response.

 diego - Support: thanks for confirming. please reopen with a new request_id if anything odd after rebuild. we'll update SPT-3399 when JOB-5602 completes. :thumbsup:
